body: Origin is not evidence. Scope note added 2026-09-24 (entry 54 §40a) — a clarification of existing meaning, not a change. This constraint governs the provenance of ideas: where an idea came from neither proves nor disproves it, in either direction. It has never governed the study of words. Origin does two jobs — where an idea came from (this constraint, A1, the ancestry audit) and where a word came from (etymology). When language is the subject, a word's history is data, governed by §1's level check and constraint 13, not by this rule. ⚠ The moment the claim leaves language, §19f's prohibition returns unchanged: no inference from shared root to shared referent, cause or jurisdiction. History is ancestry, never support.
